question.problem:
Consider the following matrices:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}5 & -4 & -2 \\ 0 & -1 & 0 \\ 4 & -4 & -1\end{aligned}],\,D=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}],\,P=[\begin{aligned}∗ & 1 & 1 \\ ∗ & 0 & 0 \\ ∗ & 2 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Given that $D={P}^{-1}AP,$ find the first column of the matrix $P.$
question.worked_solution:
From the diagonal matrix $D$, we deduce that the eigenvalues of $A$ are 

$\,$ ${\lambda }_{1}=-1,\,$ ${\lambda }_{2}=1,\,$ ${\lambda }_{3}=3.$

So, the first column of $P$ corresponds to the eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{1}=-1.$

Now, we need to find an eigenvector that corresponds to ${\lambda }_{1}=-1.$ Computing $A-(-1)I,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}A-(-1)I & =[\begin{aligned}5 & -4 & -2 \\ 0 & -1 & 0 \\ 4 & -4 & -1\end{aligned}]-(-1)[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}6 & -4 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 4 & -4 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations with the augmented matrix $M$ that we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}6 & -4 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 4 & -4 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:=\frac{1}{4}{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & -1 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}↔{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 & -1 & 0 \\ 1 & -1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-\frac{1}{3}){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & -\frac{1}{3} & \frac{1}{3} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has two pivot columns ($1$st and $2$nd). Thus, ${x}_{3}$ is a free variable. From the second equation, we obtain ${x}_{2}={x}_{3}.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we get ${x}_{1}={x}_{3}.$
Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Therefore, setting ${x}_{3}=1,$ we get the eigenvector 

$$
{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, $P=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 1\end{aligned}].$
